أول ٣٠ ثانية: الرياضة + متى بدأت + السبب اللي خلاك تبدأ
ثاني ٣٠ ثانية: كم مرة بالأسبوع، وين، وكم مدة الحصة
آخر ٣٠ ثانية: التأثير الجسدي + التأثير النفسي (سببين مختلفين)
rts.model: The activity I do regularly is swimming, and I started about three years ago, mainly because my back hurt from sitting at a desk all day and a doctor suggested it. I swim twice a week, usually on Sunday and Wednesday evenings, at a small pool ten minutes from my apartment. Each session is around forty-five minutes, and I try to do a fixed number of lengths rather than just playing in the water. About the effect, it's the clearest change I've made in years. My back pain has almost disappeared, I sleep much better on the nights I swim, and I've lost some weight without changing my food. There's also a mental part. When I'm in the water I can't check my phone or think about work, so it's the only forty-five minutes in my week when my head is completely quiet.

rts.prompt: Talk about a podcast, video channel, or radio program that you follow.
bullets: What is it about, and how did you find it?
When do you usually listen to it or watch it?
Why do you keep following it?
rts.outline_ar:
أول ٣٠ ثانية: الموضوع بجملة + كيف اكتشفته (صديق، إعلان، بحث)
ثاني ٣٠ ثانية: وقتك المعتاد + المدة وليش تناسبك
آخر ٣٠ ثانية: سببين للاستمرار (المحتوى + فايدة إضافية مثل اللغة)
rts.model: The channel I follow most is a science podcast that explains one research study every week in simple language: things like sleep, memory, exercise, or why we get bored. I found it two years ago when a colleague sent me an episode about caffeine, and I've listened almost every week since then. I usually listen in the car on the way to work, or when I'm walking in the evening, because each episode is about thirty minutes, which fits perfectly. Sometimes I put it on while I'm cooking. The reason I keep following it is that the host doesn't sell anything and doesn't exaggerate. He explains what a study actually found and, more importantly, what it doesn't prove, which is rare online. It's also good for my English, because the vocabulary is academic but the speed is comfortable.

rts.prompt: Talk about the way you organize your study or work time.
bullets: What system or routine do you use?
What do you do when you lose focus?
How well does it work for you?
rts.outline_ar:
أول ٣٠ ثانية: نظامك بجملة أو جملتين (قائمة، فترات، أصعب مهمة الصبح)
ثاني ٣٠ ثانية: وش تسوي لما تروح التركيز — خطوات عملية مو كلام عام
آخر ٣٠ ثانية: تقييم صادق بنسبة تقريبية + الدرس اللي تعلمته
rts.model: My system is fairly simple, and I built it after months of doing nothing until the night before a deadline. I write three tasks for the day on paper, not on my phone, and I work in blocks of about forty minutes with a short break between them. The hardest task always goes in the morning, because after four o'clock my brain is finished. When I lose focus, which happens a lot, I don't fight it. I stand up, drink water, walk around the building for five minutes, and put my phone in a drawer in another room, since that's usually the reason I stopped in the first place. It works reasonably well, maybe seventy percent of the time. The days it fails are the days I skip writing the list, so the list matters more than any app I've tried.

rts.prompt: Talk about a change you would like to see in your neighborhood.
bullets: What is the problem now?
What change would you like, and why?
Who could make it happen?
rts.outline_ar:
أول ٣٠ ثانية: المشكلة بتفاصيل محسوسة (شوارع ضيقة، أرض فاضية، ما فيه مكان للعيال)
ثاني ٣٠ ثانية: التغيير المحدد + فايدتين منه
آخر ٣٠ ثانية: مين المسؤول ووش الخطوة الواقعية الأولى
rts.model: The main problem in my neighborhood is that there's nowhere safe for children to play. The streets are narrow, cars park on both sides, and the only open space is a piece of empty land full of sand and trash. So the kids play football between the cars, which honestly worries me every time I drive in. The change I'd like is simple: turn that empty land into a small park with grass, some trees, lights, and a fence. Trees would also help with the heat, because our street has almost no shade in summer. As for who could make it happen, the municipality owns the land, so the decision is theirs, but I don't think anything will move unless the residents ask together. A few neighbors have already collected signatures, and a local company might pay for part of it.

rts.prompt: Talk about a time you saved money for something you wanted.
bullets: What were you saving for, and why?
How did you save the money?
Was it worth it in the end?
rts.outline_ar:
أول ٣٠ ثانية: وش الشي اللي جمعت له + ليش صار ضرورة مو رغبة
ثاني ٣٠ ثانية: طريقتك بالتوفير (حساب منفصل، مبلغ ثابت، عادات وقفتها)
آخر ٣٠ ثانية: جاوب بوضوح: يستاهل ولا لا + دليل واحد
rts.model: A few years ago I saved for a good laptop, because I was studying and working with an old one that took five minutes to open a file and switched itself off during video calls. It was becoming a real problem, not just a wish. The way I saved was boring but effective. I opened a separate account and moved a fixed amount into it on the first day of every month, before I spent anything, and I stopped two habits: buying coffee outside and ordering food at night. I also sold my old phone and put that money in as well, so after about seven months I had enough. Was it worth it? Definitely. The laptop is four years old now and still fast, and it paid for itself, because I could take freelance design work in the evenings.

questions.q: Let's start by talking about money. How do you usually decide what to spend your money on each month?
questions.model: Honestly, I decide in a very simple way. The reason is that I don't enjoy tracking every single purchase, so I use a rough rule instead. For example, at the start of the month I move part of my salary into savings, then I pay the fixed things like rent and my phone, and whatever is left is for food and going out.
questions.tip_ar: جاوب بطريقتك الحقيقية حتى لو بسيطة — الصدق مع تفصيل أقوى من كلام مثالي عام.

questions.q: Now let's think more generally. Do you think young people in your country are good at saving money?
questions.model: In my opinion, most young people are not very good at it, although it's improving. The main reason is that nobody teaches it. We study mathematics for twelve years but never learn about budgets, saving, or debt. For example, most of my friends knew how to buy a phone in twenty-four payments before they knew how much it cost in total.
questions.tip_ar: استخدم 'most young people' مو 'all' — التعميم المعتدل يبان أذكى ويعطيك مجال للاستدراك.

questions.q: Here's a harder question. Some people say that talking openly about salaries would make workplaces fairer. Do you agree?
questions.model: I agree, to a large extent. The reason is that secrecy usually protects the company, not the employee. When nobody knows what anyone earns, two people can do exactly the same job for very different money and never find out. For example, a friend of mine discovered after three years that a new colleague was earning more than her for the same role.
questions.tip_ar: 'to a large extent' تعطيك موقف واضح مع مرونة، وبعدين اعترف بعيب واحد بس لا تغيّر رأيك.

questions.q: Let's change topics now and talk about advertising. Where do you usually see or hear advertisements?
questions.model: Mostly on my phone, unfortunately. The reason is that I don't watch much television, so almost everything reaches me through apps. For example, I see short video ads between clips, sponsored posts from people I follow, and emails from a shop where I bought something once, three years ago. I also notice the big screens along the main road when I'm driving.
questions.tip_ar: تغيير الموضوع مفاجئ — لا ترجع تتكلم عن الفلوس، ادخل على الإعلانات مباشرة.

questions.q: Thinking about society, how has advertising changed compared with twenty years ago?
questions.model: I think the biggest change is that advertising now knows who you are. Twenty years ago everyone watching the same channel saw the same commercial, but today two people can open the same app and see completely different products. For example, after I searched once for running shoes, they followed me around the internet for weeks.
questions.tip_ar: قارن 'twenty years ago' مقابل 'today' بجملتين متوازيتين — أسهل طريقة تبين فيها تغيّر.

questions.q: Finally, do you think there should be stricter rules on advertising aimed at children?
questions.model: Yes, I feel quite strongly about this. The reason is that children can't really judge what they're being shown; they simply want it. For example, my nephew is six, and after watching one video he asked for the same toy for a month, even though he didn't understand what it did. I'd limit ads during children's programs and label paid videos clearly.
questions.tip_ar: اختم بحل وسط عملي (تحديد مو منع) — يبيّن إنك تفكر مو بس تتحمس.

questions.q: Let's begin with public transport. How often do you use buses or trains in your city?
questions.model: Honestly, almost never, and I wish the answer were different. The reason is that we don't really have a network; there are a few bus lines, but they come every forty minutes and none of them passes near my house. For example, last month I tried to reach a meeting downtown by bus, and the trip took over an hour compared with twenty minutes by car.
questions.tip_ar: لو جوابك 'أبداً' لا تسكت — اشرح السبب بمثال ورقم، وبكذا تصير إجابة كاملة.

questions.q: More generally, what stops people in your country from using public transport?
questions.model: I think the main reason is that it's seen as transport for people who have no other choice. Some families judge you a little if you take the bus, and an idea like that is hard to remove. The second reason is practical: no shade at the stops, no reliable timetable, and terrible heat in summer.
questions.tip_ar: رتب سببين بوضوح: 'the main reason' ثم 'the second reason' — الترتيب يرفع درجة التنظيم.

questions.q: Here's a bigger question. Do you think governments should make driving more expensive in order to reduce traffic?
questions.model: I agree, but only after the alternative exists. The reason is that a tax on driving without a good metro simply punishes people who have no other option, especially those with low salaries. For example, some cities charge cars entering the center, and it works there because there's a train every four minutes. So I'd build first and charge second.
questions.tip_ar: 'I agree, but only if/after…' جواب قوي بالأسئلة السياسية — موقف واضح مع شرط.

questions.q: Let's turn to driving now. When did you learn to drive, and what do you remember about it?
questions.model: I learned at eighteen, mostly with my older brother in an empty parking area before I took proper lessons. What I remember is how tiring it was at the beginning. I'd arrive home after thirty minutes completely exhausted, because I was thinking about every single movement. For example, I once stopped in the middle of a roundabout and my brother didn't speak to me for a while.
questions.tip_ar: ذكرى صغيرة ومضحكة تخلي الجواب طبيعي — الممتحن يقيم اللغة مو بطولاتك.

questions.q: Thinking about society, what are the main causes of accidents on the roads where you live?
questions.model: In my opinion, the biggest cause is speed combined with phones. The reason is that our roads are wide and straight, which makes drivers relaxed, and then they look down to answer a message. For example, I see people holding a phone at a hundred kilometers an hour almost every day. Weak enforcement makes it worse, because a small fine changes nothing.
questions.tip_ar: اذكر سببين مترابطين (سرعة + جوال) بدل قائمة طويلة — العمق أفضل من العدد.

questions.q: Finally, do you think self-driving cars will make roads safer in the future?
questions.model: I think they will, eventually, but the middle period worries me. The reason is that machines don't get tired, angry, or distracted, and those three things cause most accidents. For example, a computer would never send a message while driving. However, mixing human drivers and automatic ones on the same road is complicated, because people do unpredictable things.
questions.tip_ar: في أسئلة المستقبل استخدم 'eventually' و'in the long run' — تعطيك دقة بدون ما تلتزم بتاريخ.

questions.q: Let's start with studying. Where and when do you usually study best?
questions.model: I study best early in the morning, at the desk in my bedroom, with the door closed. The reason is that my head is clear before I read any messages, and nobody at home is awake yet. For example, when I was preparing for a certificate last year, I woke at five and learned more in those two hours than in a whole evening.
questions.tip_ar: حدد المكان والوقت بدقة (الساعة ٥، مكتب الغرفة) — التفاصيل الصغيرة ترفع الدرجة.

questions.q: Now more generally. Do you think students in your country study in an effective way?
questions.model: I don't think so, in most cases. The main reason is that our system rewards memorizing rather than understanding, so students learn the answer instead of the idea. For example, at school I could repeat the definition of photosynthesis perfectly and still not explain why a plant needs light. University is better, with projects and presentations, but the school habit is hard to break.
questions.tip_ar: مثال محسوس من مادة معينة أقوى من كلمة 'التعليم عندنا ضعيف' بمليون مرة.

questions.q: Here's a harder one. Some people say that studying in a group is a waste of time. What do you think?
questions.model: I'd say it depends completely on the stage. The reason is that group study is excellent for testing what you already know and terrible for learning something new. For example, when my friends and I met to explain topics to each other before an exam, I discovered my gaps immediately. But the meetings where we tried to read new material together always turned into conversation and coffee.
questions.tip_ar: 'It depends on…' مقبول بس بشرط تحدد على وش يعتمد بجملة وحدة واضحة.

questions.q: Let's move on to exams. How do you usually feel before an important test?
questions.model: Quite nervous, especially the night before. The reason is mostly physical: I can't sleep properly, and then I worry about not sleeping, which is worse than the exam itself. For example, before my driving test I lay awake until three in the morning. What helps me is preparing everything the evening before, the documents, the clothes, the route, so my mind has fewer things to hold.
questions.tip_ar: وصف الإحساس بالجسم (ما أنام، قلق) أطبع من 'I feel stressed' لحالها.

questions.q: Thinking more broadly, do exams really show a student's ability?
questions.model: Only partly, in my opinion. The reason is that an exam measures performance on one morning under pressure, which suits some people and destroys others. For example, a friend of mine understood chemistry better than anyone in our class, but he froze in the exam hall and got an average grade. I'd keep exams, but the final grade should also include projects done during the year.
questions.tip_ar: 'Only partly' + سبب + مثال = جواب متوازن، ولا تنسى تقترح البديل.

questions.q: Finally, if you could change one thing about the way students are tested, what would it be?
questions.model: I'd reduce the weight of the final exam and spread it across the year. The reason is that one three-hour paper deciding a whole year encourages memorizing and panic, not real learning. For example, in one of my university courses the grade came from four small assignments and a presentation, and I still remember that material today, years later.
questions.tip_ar: سؤال 'one thing' يبي تغيير واحد محدد — لا تعطي ثلاثة، وطوّل بالتبرير بدلها.

questions.q: Let's start with the news. How do you usually follow what is happening in the world?
questions.model: Mostly on my phone, in short pieces. The reason is time: I don't sit and watch a bulletin at nine o'clock the way my parents do. For example, I check two news apps in the morning with my coffee, and if something big happens I look for a longer article in the evening. I also get links from friends, which isn't the most reliable way.
questions.tip_ar: قارن نفسك بجيل أهلك بجملة قصيرة — طريقة سهلة تضيف عمق بدون فلسفة.

questions.q: More generally, do people in your country trust the news they read?
questions.model: I'd say trust is quite low, and it's still falling. The main reason is the speed of social media: a story spreads for two days, and then somebody proves it was false, so people remember the feeling more than the correction. For example, during the last big storm, half the videos in my family group turned out to be old clips from another country.
questions.tip_ar: اختم بملاحظة إيجابية غير متوقعة — تبيّن إنك تحلل مو بس تشتكي.

questions.q: Here's a bigger question. Should news be free, or should people pay for good journalism?
questions.model: I believe people should pay, even though nobody wants to. The reason is that serious reporting is expensive: somebody has to travel, investigate, and check facts for weeks. If all news is free, it will be paid for by advertising, and then articles get written to attract clicks. For example, the free sites I read are full of shocking headlines and very little detail.
questions.tip_ar: خذ الموقف غير الشعبي إذا تقدر تدافع عنه — الوضوح أهم من إرضاء السؤال.

questions.q: Let's change topics and talk about influencers. Do you follow anyone on social media regularly?
questions.model: Yes, but mainly practical accounts rather than famous people. The reason is that I want to learn something specific. For example, I follow a mechanic who explains car problems in two-minute videos, and a woman who reviews kitchen equipment honestly, including when a product is bad. In short, I follow accounts that teach me something useful, not accounts that are just famous.
questions.tip_ar: 'Yes, but…' افتتاحية ممتازة: تجاوب السؤال فورًا وتفتح لك مجال تفصّل.

questions.q: Thinking about society, how do influencers affect the way young people spend money?
questions.model: I think the effect is strong and mostly negative. The reason is that an advertisement from a person you watch every day doesn't feel like an advertisement; it feels like advice from a friend. For example, my younger cousin bought an expensive skincare product because someone she likes recommended it, and she never asked whether it was a paid promotion.
questions.tip_ar: مثال من العائلة (بنت خالتي، ولد عمي) أسرع طريقة تجيب مثال حقيقي تحت الضغط.

questions.q: Finally, should influencers be responsible for the products they promote?
questions.model: Absolutely, and I'd make it a legal responsibility. The reason is that they're paid exactly because their audience trusts them, so that trust is the real product they're selling. For example, if someone promotes a financial app and people lose money, saying it was just an advertisement isn't good enough. Honest mistakes are fine, but hiding that you were paid should have consequences.
questions.tip_ar: لو رأيك قوي ابدأ بـ 'Absolutely' وبعدين هدّي الجواب بشرط — قوة مع اتزان.

questions.q: Let's begin with sleep. What does a normal night look like for you?
questions.model: Not as good as it should be, honestly. The reason is that I go to bed late even when I'm tired, usually around one in the morning, because the evening is the only time that feels like mine. For example, I finish work, eat, spend time with my family, and only at eleven do I finally sit down and watch something.
questions.tip_ar: ما يلزم تعطي جواب مثالي — الاعتراف بعادة سيئة مع شرح سببها يبان طبيعي وقوي.

questions.q: More generally, do you think people today sleep less than in the past?
questions.model: Definitely, and I think the phone is the main reason. Before, when the television programs ended, the day was over. Now there's always one more video. For example, my grandfather still sleeps at nine and wakes before sunrise without an alarm, while nobody in my generation does that. Work has changed too: many people answer messages at midnight, so the day never really closes.
questions.tip_ar: جملة 'the day never really closes' نوع من التعبير الطبيعي — احفظ تراكيب قصيرة مثلها.

questions.q: Here's a harder question. Some companies now let employees start work later in the day. Is that a good idea?
questions.model: I support it strongly. The reason is that people are genuinely different: some are sharp at seven in the morning and useless after three, and for others it's the opposite. Forcing everybody into the same hours wastes half of that energy. For example, I'd produce much better work between ten and seven than between seven and four.
questions.tip_ar: اختم بشرط عملي ('the only condition is…') — يخلي جوابك يبدو مدروس مو متحمس.

questions.q: Let's talk about stress now. What makes you feel stressed, and how do you notice it?
questions.model: The main thing is having several unfinished tasks at the same time. The way I notice it is physical: my shoulders get tight and I become impatient with people at home for no reason. For example, during a very busy month last year I snapped at my brother over something tiny, and that's usually my signal that the problem isn't him, it's my workload.
questions.tip_ar: السؤال فيه جزئين (وش يسبب + كيف تلاحظ) — جاوب الاثنين بوضوح ولا تنسى الثاني.

questions.q: Thinking about society, why do stress levels seem higher than in the past?
questions.model: In my opinion, it's because work no longer has a clear end. The reason is that we all carry the office in our pocket, so there's no moment when nobody can reach you. For example, my father left his job at three o'clock and that was genuinely finished until the next morning. Add housing costs and constant comparison online, and people always feel behind.
questions.tip_ar: اجمع سببين مختلفين (تقنية + اقتصاد) بجملة وحدة في الآخر — يعطي إحساس بالإحاطة.

questions.q: Finally, what advice would you give to someone who feels stressed all the time?
questions.model: I'd say start with the body before the mind. The reason is that advice such as telling someone to think positively is very hard to follow when you're exhausted. For example, when I fixed my sleep and started walking forty minutes a day, my problems didn't disappear, but they stopped feeling impossible. After that, write everything down so it's outside your head.
questions.tip_ar: في أسئلة النصيحة استخدم 'I'd say…' وأعط نصيحتين مرتبتين، ثم تحذير أخير قصير.

questions.q: Let's start with your neighbors. Do you know the people who live near you?
questions.model: Some of them, yes. The reason is that we've been in the same building for about eight years, so you can't avoid people completely. For example, I know the family on our floor quite well; we exchange food during the holidays and they keep our keys when we travel. But the apartments upstairs change every year, and honestly I couldn't tell you a single name.
questions.tip_ar: جواب 'بعضهم' أصدق من نعم أو لا — وبعدين وضّح الفرق بين الحالتين.

questions.q: More generally, do you think neighbors are less close than they used to be?
questions.model: Yes, clearly, at least in the cities. The main reason is how we live now: tall buildings, closed doors, and everybody leaving early and coming back late. For example, my mother grew up in a small street where the doors were open and children ate in any house, and she finds our building strange and cold.
questions.tip_ar: قصة أمك أو جدك عن الماضي = مثال جاهز لأي سؤال عن 'كيف تغيّر المجتمع'.

questions.q: Here's a bigger question. What could make people in a neighborhood feel more connected?
questions.model: I think the answer is shared physical space, more than any app. The reason is that connection happens when people meet by accident, not when they plan it. For example, in the area where my uncle lives there's a small park with benches, and the older men meet there every evening without arranging anything. So parks, a local market, a community hall.
questions.tip_ar: لما تعطي حل، عارض حل شائع ('more than any app') — المقارنة تقوي وجهة نظرك.

questions.q: Let's move on to volunteering. Have you ever done any volunteer work?
questions.model: Yes, a few times, mostly during university. The reason I started was simply that a friend needed help and I went with him. For example, we spent several weekends packing food boxes for families, and one summer I helped organize a blood donation day at the college. I don't do it regularly now, but I try to give a few days every year.
questions.tip_ar: اذكر نشاطين ملموسين بأسمائهم — أفضل من 'ساعدت الناس' العامة.

questions.q: Thinking about society, why do you think some people never volunteer?
questions.model: I think the main reason is that they don't know how to start, rather than not caring. The organizations aren't visible, and people imagine that it requires a huge commitment. For example, several colleagues told me they would help if somebody simply told them where and when. Time is real too: if you work six days a week and have children, a free Saturday is precious.
questions.tip_ar: افترض حسن النية بالناس ('rather than not caring') — جواب ناضج وسهل تدافع عنه.

questions.q: Finally, should schools require students to do a certain number of volunteer hours?
questions.model: I agree with the idea, with one condition. The reason is that most people never try volunteering unless something pushes them, and once they've done it, some of them continue for life. For example, a cousin of mine started because of a school requirement, and now she works with a charity every month. The condition is that it must be real work, not just signing a paper.
questions.tip_ar: 'I agree, with one condition' تركيب سريع يعطيك موقف + عمق في ٥ ثواني.

questions.q: Let's begin with science. Were you interested in science subjects at school?
questions.model: Yes, especially physics and biology, although I wasn't a top student. The reason is that they explained things I could actually see: why the sky changes color, how the heart works. For example, I still remember an experiment where we measured how fast a pulse recovers after exercise, and I went home and tested my whole family. Chemistry I never enjoyed, mostly because it felt like memorizing tables.
questions.tip_ar: قل وش حبيت ووش ما حبيت — التباين يعطي مادة للكلام ويبان صادق.

questions.q: More generally, why do you think fewer young people choose scientific careers?
questions.model: I think the main reason is money and time. A science degree is long and difficult, and then a researcher often earns less than somebody in business or marketing. For example, a friend of mine finished a master's in chemistry and now works in sales, because the salary was double. So unless research pays better, the best students will keep leaving it.
questions.tip_ar: سببين كفاية (فلوس + صورة ذهنية) وكل واحد بمثال — لا تعدد خمسة بدون شرح.

questions.q: Here's a bigger question. Some people say space exploration is a waste of money. Do you agree?
questions.model: I disagree, although I understand the argument. The reason is that space research produces technology we use every day: satellites for weather and communication, medical imaging, better water filters. For example, the maps on our phones only exist because of satellites. Of course there are urgent problems on Earth, but space budgets are tiny compared with what governments spend elsewhere, so stopping them wouldn't solve poverty.
questions.tip_ar: اعترف بالرأي المعارض بجملة ('I understand the argument') قبل ما ترد — يرفع درجتك.

questions.q: Let's change topics and talk about artificial intelligence. Do you use AI tools in your daily life?
questions.model: Yes, more than I expected a year ago. The reason is that they save real time on boring tasks. For example, I use one to summarize long documents at work, and to check my English before I send an important email. I also use translation constantly, although I always check the result before I trust it. In short, they save me time every day.
questions.tip_ar: 'more than I expected' افتتاحية طبيعية جدًا، وأضف حد واحد تتجنبه — يبيّن وعي.

questions.q: Thinking about work, how do you think AI will change jobs in the next ten years?
questions.model: I think it will change most jobs rather than delete them, but some will definitely disappear. The reason is that these tools are good at repeated tasks with clear rules: basic translation, simple reports, first-level customer service. For example, a friend who worked in data entry now checks what the software produced instead of typing it himself.
questions.tip_ar: في أسئلة المستقبل استخدم 'rather than' للتمييز بين تغيير وإلغاء — دقة تفكير.

questions.q: Finally, do you think there should be international rules for artificial intelligence?
questions.model: Yes, although I'm not optimistic about how well they would work. The reason is that the technology crosses borders instantly, so a rule in one country means very little. For example, a company can simply build its system somewhere with weaker regulation. I'd focus on clear basics: labeling generated content and keeping a human responsible for big decisions.
questions.tip_ar: لو الموضوع كبير، ضيّقه بنفسك ('I'd focus on…') بدل ما تحاول تغطي كل شي.

questions.q: Let's start with clothes. How do you usually choose what to wear?
questions.model: Very quickly, honestly. The reason is that I decided years ago to keep a simple wardrobe so that mornings are easy. For example, most of my shirts are plain and in three colors, so almost anything matches and I don't have to think about it. The main thing I consider is the weather and whether I have meetings that day.
questions.tip_ar: النهاية الخفيفة المضحكة مسموحة وتخلي كلامك يبان محكي مو محفوظ.

questions.q: More generally, is fashion important to people in your country?
questions.model: I'd say appearance matters a lot, more than fashion in the international sense. The reason is that clothes are part of respect here: you dress well for guests, for work, and especially for family occasions. For example, my cousin will spend a month's savings on an outfit for a wedding without hesitating. Younger people follow global trends now, but looking neat still matters more.
questions.tip_ar: فرّق بين مصطلحين ('appearance' مقابل 'fashion') — التمييز الدقيق بين المصطلحين علامة مستوى B2 فأعلى.

questions.q: Here's a harder question. The clothing industry produces a lot of waste. Whose responsibility is it to fix that?
questions.model: I think it's mainly the companies, with governments pushing them. The reason is that individuals can't choose what doesn't exist: if every cheap shirt is designed to last six months, buying carefully becomes very difficult. For example, I have a jacket from a small brand that's ten years old, but it cost four times more than a normal one.
questions.tip_ar: في أسئلة المسؤولية حدد الطرف الرئيسي ثم أضف الطرف المساعد — مو 'الكل مسؤول'.

questions.q: Let's change topics and talk about used items. Have you ever bought something second-hand?
questions.model: Yes, several times, and usually the experience was good. The reason is price: some things lose half their value the moment somebody opens the box. For example, I bought my desk and two bookshelves from a family that was moving abroad, and I paid about a third of the shop price for better wood. I also bought a used bicycle once.
questions.tip_ar: استثناء واحد في الآخر ('the only thing I wouldn't…') يعطي شخصية ورأي واضح.

questions.q: Thinking about society, why do some people avoid buying used items?
questions.model: I think it's partly about image and partly about trust. The image part is that in many families buying used suggests you can't afford new, which people find embarrassing. For example, my aunt refuses even to look at second-hand furniture. The trust part is more reasonable: with electronics you can't see the history, there's no guarantee, and if it stops working after a week, nobody will help you.
questions.tip_ar: 'partly… and partly…' تركيب ممتاز لما يكون فيه سببين مختلفين بالطبيعة.

questions.q: Finally, do you think companies should be required to make products easier to repair?
questions.model: Yes, I feel strongly about this. The reason is that a lot of things are now designed so that repair is impossible, or costs almost as much as a replacement. For example, my washing machine failed after four years, and the technician told me the part alone was two thirds of the price of a new machine, so we threw it away.
questions.tip_ar: مثال بأرقام تقريبية ('two thirds of the price') يقنع أكثر من وصف عام.

sample.prompt: Describe a problem you solved at work or at university. What was the problem, what did you do, and what was the result?
sample.plan_ar:
١) وصف المشكلة برقم أو أثر واضح (كنا نخسر طلبات ومحد يعرف ليش)
٢) السبب الحقيقي اللي اكتشفته (البطء بالرد ومروره على ٣ أشخاص)
٣) وش سويت بالضبط + كيف أقنعتهم (أرقام مو شكاوى)
٤) النتيجة + الدرس
sample.model:
I'd like to talk about a problem I solved last year at work, because it's the one I'm most proud of. I work in a small company that sells equipment to clinics, and we kept losing orders. Customers would call, ask for a price, and then simply disappear, and nobody really understood why.

The problem was that our answers were slow. When a customer asked for a quotation, the request went to the sales team, then to the warehouse to check the stock, then to my manager for a discount, and the whole thing took four or five days. By that time the customer had already bought from somebody faster.

What I did was quite simple. I spent a week writing down every step and how long it took, with real dates, and I presented the numbers in a meeting instead of just complaining. Then I suggested two changes: a shared sheet showing our stock in real time, and permission for the sales team to give a small discount without asking anyone.

My manager agreed to try it for two months. Our average answer time dropped from about four days to one, and we won several orders that we would definitely have lost before. What I learned is that people accept a change much more easily when you bring numbers instead of opinions.

sample.prompt: Talk about the changes you would make to your city if you were the mayor. What would you change first, and why?
sample.plan_ar:
١) قل إن عندك ثلاث أولويات ورتبها
٢) الأولوية الأولى: النقل — ليش وبأي حل عملي (مسارات باصات أرخص من مترو)
٣) الأولوية الثانية: الظل والحدائق — اربطها بالحر
٤) الأولوية الثالثة صغيرة بس شخصية (تطبيق للبلاغات) واختم بفكرة واحدة
sample.model:
If I were the mayor of my city, I'd have a very long list, but I'd start with three things.

The first thing I'd change is public transport. At the moment almost everybody drives, because the buses are slow and there's no metro, so the main roads are blocked for two hours every morning. I'd put real money into bus lanes first, since they're much cheaper and faster to build than a train line, and I'd make the timetable something people can actually trust.

The second change would be shade and green space. My city is extremely hot for five months of the year, and walking anywhere between ten and four is almost impossible. Planting trees along the main streets and building a small park in every neighborhood would change daily life more than any big project. Children would have somewhere to play, and older people could walk in the evening.

The third thing is smaller, but it matters to me: the way the municipality answers residents. Right now, if a street light is broken or there's a hole in the road, nobody knows who to call. I'd create one simple app where you send a photo and receive a reference number and a date.

None of this is exciting, but I believe a city works when the boring things work.

sample.prompt: Describe a photograph or a video that means a lot to you. What is in it, and why is it important?
sample.plan_ar:
١) وين الصورة ومتى تشوفها
٢) وصف بصري: مين فيها، وش لابسين، وش وراهم، وش تسوي أنت
٣) ليش مهمة: سببين — اليوم نفسه + اللي صار بعدين
٤) اختم بجملة عن الدرس أو الشعور
sample.model:
The photograph I want to describe is on the wall in my parents' living room, and I look at it every time I visit them.

It was taken about fifteen years ago, at the end of a school trip to the mountains. In the picture there are around twenty of us standing on some rocks, all wearing the same blue jackets that the school gave us, and you can actually see clouds below us, because we were quite high up. I'm on the right side, laughing at something, and my best friend at that time has his arm around my shoulder. What I love about it is that nobody is posing properly. Half the group is looking in the wrong direction.

The reason it means so much to me is partly the day itself, which was the first time I had ever seen snow, and partly what happened afterwards. That group of friends separated after graduation. Some moved to other cities, one of them lives in Canada now, and two of them I haven't spoken to in years, not because of any problem, just life.

So the photo is really a picture of a moment when we all still believed we would stay together. It reminds me to make an effort with the people I care about, because distance happens very quietly.

sample.prompt: Talk about the advantages and disadvantages of living far from your family. How does it affect daily life?
sample.plan_ar:
١) قل إن عندك تجربة شخصية وكم صار لك
٢) الإيجابيات: استقلال + فرص عمل + علاقة أهدأ مع الأهل
٣) السلبيات: الأيام العادية مو المناسبات، وتفوتك أشياء ما ترجع
٤) التأثير اليومي (تخطيط، تذاكر، مكالمات) واختم برأي متوازن
sample.model:
I've lived far from my family for about six years now, so this is a subject I know well, and honestly it has two very different sides.

The advantages are real. Living alone in another city forced me to become independent much faster. I had to manage my own money, cook, deal with a landlord, and solve problems without asking anybody. I also had opportunities that I simply couldn't have had at home, because the jobs in my field are all in bigger cities. And there's a strange benefit that people don't often mention: my relationship with my parents actually improved, because when we do meet, nobody is arguing about small daily things.

The disadvantages are heavier than I expected. The hardest part is the ordinary days, not the holidays. Nobody notices when you're sick, and eating alone every evening becomes tiring after a few years. You also miss things you can't get back. My sister's children are growing up, and I see them three times a year, so they know me as a visitor.

In daily life it means I plan everything: flights, holidays, a video call every Friday. I don't regret the decision at all, but I understand now that it has a price, and you pay it slowly.

sample.prompt: Describe something you own that you have had for a long time. What is it, and why have you kept it?
sample.plan_ar:
١) الشيء + كم لك محتفظ فيه
٢) وصف دقيق: اللون، الحجم، العيوب الصغيرة (خدوش، يتأخر دقيقتين)
٣) القصة: من وين جاك ومين كان يستخدمه
٤) ليش محتفظ فيه (مو القيمة المادية) + متى تستخدمه
sample.model:
The thing I want to talk about is a watch that belonged to my father, which I've had for about twelve years now.

It isn't expensive at all. It's a simple steel watch with a white face and a brown leather strap, and the glass has two small scratches on the left side. It doesn't even work perfectly; it loses about two minutes every week, so I have to correct it. I've changed the strap three times, but everything else is exactly as it was.

My father wore it every day when he worked as a teacher, and he gave it to me when I finished university. I remember that he said something very simple, something like: this one always got me to class on time.

The reason I've kept it is obviously not the value. If I sold it, I doubt anybody would give me much for it. I keep it because it's the only object in my house that carries a story I was part of. In a world where I change my phone every three years and throw things away without thinking, having one object that has survived twenty-five years feels important.

I wear it on days that matter: interviews, exams, family occasions. And when I'm nervous, I notice that I keep touching it.

sample.prompt: Talk about how people in your country deal with the hot summer. What do they do, and how has this changed?
sample.plan_ar:
١) ابدأ بالأرقام: كم الحرارة بالصيف
٢) كيف اليوم ينقلب (الشوارع فاضية بالنهار، الحياة بالليل)
٣) البيوت: مكيفات، فواتير، ضيافة بارد
٤) السفر للهروب من الحر
٥) المقارنة مع جيل الأجداد + رأيك بالنهاية
sample.model:
Summer where I live is extremely hot, usually above forty-five degrees in July and August, so people organize their whole lives around it.

The most obvious thing is that the day turns upside down. The streets are almost empty between eleven and four, and everything social happens after sunset. Families go out at nine or ten at night, children play outside at eleven, and restaurants are busiest close to midnight. Many shops close in the afternoon and open again in the evening.

At home, the air conditioning runs almost continuously, which makes electricity bills the main summer complaint. People also drink far more, and there's a strong habit of offering cold water or juice to anybody who arrives at your door.

Those who can afford it travel. A lot of families leave for a month to somewhere cooler, and the schools are closed anyway.

What has changed is interesting. My grandparents' generation slept on the roof, used thick walls and small windows, and kept water cool in clay jars. Today we depend completely on machines, so a power cut for two hours in August is a serious emergency, not an inconvenience.

So I'd say we've become much more comfortable but far less able to survive the heat without electricity, and with summers getting hotter, that worries me.

sample.prompt: Describe a mistake you made that taught you something important. What happened, and what did you learn?
sample.plan_ar:
١) متى ووين صار الخطأ (أول وظيفة، قبل ٥ سنوات)
٢) وش سويت بالضبط ووش السبب (استعجال ونسخ تقرير قديم)
٣) النتيجة والإحراج (المدير راجع ٦ شهور قدام العميل)
٤) درسين تعلمتهم + القاعدة اللي تطبقها اليوم
sample.model:
The mistake I remember most clearly happened in my first job, about five years ago, and I still think about it.

I was responsible for sending a monthly report to a client. One month I was very busy, so I copied the previous report, changed the numbers quickly, and sent it without checking. The problem was that I forgot to change the date and two figures in the middle of a table. The client noticed, of course, and then asked my manager whether the earlier reports had been correct as well.

The result was uncomfortable. My manager had to spend an entire afternoon going through six months of work with me, in front of the client, just to prove that everything else was fine. Nobody shouted at me, which somehow made it worse. He simply said that it had become a trust problem, not a mistake problem.

What I learned has stayed with me. First, small errors in a document damage confidence in everything around them, even the parts that are perfect. Second, the ten minutes I saved cost about eight hours of other people's time.

Since then I have a rule: I never send anything important immediately. I write it, do something else for twenty minutes, and read it again. It sounds simple, but it has saved me many times.

sample.prompt: Talk about the role of doctors and hospitals in your country. What works well, and what should be improved?
sample.plan_ar:
١) قل إنك بتتكلم عن الجانبين
٢) اللي يشتغل زين: الطوارئ، التغطية، الأجهزة، التطعيمات
٣) اللي يحتاج تحسين: مواعيد الاستشاريين، غياب طبيب الأسرة، الطوارئ مزحومة بحالات بسيطة
٤) فرق المدن عن القرى
٥) تغيير واحد لو بيدك + جملة ختامية
sample.model:
I'd like to talk about healthcare in my country, and I'll be honest about both sides.

What works well is access in an emergency. If something serious happens, an ambulance comes and the hospital treats you, and for citizens most of the cost is covered by the government. The equipment in the big city hospitals is genuinely modern, and many of the doctors have trained abroad. Vaccination programs for children are also well organized; my sister never had to fight for an appointment.

What should be improved is everything that happens before the emergency. Getting a normal appointment with a specialist can take weeks, and family doctors are not really part of our culture, so people go straight to the hospital for small problems. That fills the emergency department with cases that don't belong there. I once waited four hours with a simple infection.

The second problem is the difference between cities and small towns. In a village you might have one clinic with a single doctor, so people drive two hours for a basic test.

If I could change one thing, I'd build a strong network of local clinics, so that hospitals only handle serious cases. Prevention is much cheaper than treatment, and at the moment we spend most of our money at the wrong end.

sample.prompt: Describe an app or a website you would like someone to create. What problem would it solve, and who would use it?
sample.plan_ar:
١) الفكرة بجملة وحدة واضحة
٢) المشكلة الحالية بمثال شخصي (غرامة نسيت تجديدها)
٣) الخصائص: مواعيد، صور مستندات، تكاليف، تنبيهات
٤) الميزة الأقوى (سجل كامل عند البيع والشراء)
٥) مين المستخدم المستهدف
sample.model:
The app I'd like somebody to create is one that manages everything about a car in a single place, because at the moment this information is scattered everywhere.

The problem is simple. My car needs an oil change every few months, insurance once a year, an inspection, and various repairs. All of that lives in paper receipts in my glove box, a message from a garage somewhere in my phone, and my memory, which is not reliable at all. Twice I've paid a fine because I forgot a renewal date.

So the app would keep a record for each car: the dates, the documents as photos, what was repaired and how much it cost, and it would remind me two weeks before anything expires. I'd also like a section showing the total I've spent this year, because honestly I have no idea.

The most useful feature, though, would be the history when buying or selling. If I could show a complete service record when I sell my car, and read one before I buy, that would change the used-car market completely.

Who would use it? Anybody who owns a car, but especially people like me who are not mechanical, and small companies with five or ten vehicles that currently use paper.

sample.prompt: Talk about how young people choose their career today compared with their parents' generation.
sample.plan_ar:
١) قل إن الفرق كبير وإنك تشوفه في عائلتك
٢) جيل الآباء: قائمة قصيرة، الهدف الأمان، تغيير الوظيفة عيب
٣) جيلنا: وظائف ما كانت موجودة، تغيير المسار عادي، البحث عن معنى ومرونة
٤) التكلفة: حيرة ومقارنة على السوشال ميديا
٥) جملة موازنة أخيرة (أمان بلا حرية مقابل حرية بلا أمان)
sample.model:
I think the way young people choose a career today is very different from their parents' generation, and I see this clearly in my own family.

My father's generation had a short list. You became a teacher, a doctor, an engineer, a government employee, or you worked in the family business. The main goal was security: a stable salary, a pension, and the same office for thirty years. Nobody really asked whether the work was interesting, and changing jobs often looked like a sign of failure.

Today the list is much longer and much less clear. My friends work in fields that didn't exist when we were children: data analysis, digital marketing, content creation. Several of them changed direction completely at twenty-eight. The questions people ask are different too. They want work that has some meaning, flexible hours, and often the possibility of working remotely.

There's a cost, though. More choice creates more confusion and much more comparison, especially because social media shows everybody's success and nobody's difficulties. A lot of young people I know feel that they're already late at twenty-five, which is ridiculous.

So I'd say our parents had security without freedom, and we have freedom without security. Personally I prefer our situation, but I think we underestimate how stressful it is.
